instruction: Write a Sounio run-pass example named `dissertation_pbpk28_confidence_gate`. PBPK28 rapamycin priors carried as Knowledge<f64> with literature ε. It should compile and run successfully.
description: PBPK28 rapamycin priors carried as Knowledge<f64> with literature ε.
comments: These are the real rapamycin priors from stdlib/darwin_pbpk/epistemic_pbpk28.sio
(ep28_rapamycin_priors), where confidence was a plain f64 the type system could
not see. Carried as Knowledge<f64, ε> they become first-class: the ε flows into
the EpistemicComplete gate, so a function cannot claim more confidence than its
weakest input supports.
cl_hepatic ε=0.65 (Jiao/Zhang 2009 pop-PK, CV≈38%)
fu_plasma  ε=0.72 (Schreiber 1991, CV≈25%)
kp_liver   ε=0.60 (Valoteau 1996, CV≈25%)
kp_adipose ε=0.40 (capped model, CV≈40%)   ← the weakest evidence
Gate semantics (per-token, NOT combined): `with Epistemic(N)` requires EVERY
input expression to individually carry confidence ≥ N. It does NOT certify the
propagated/combined confidence of the result (that compounds far lower). So the
maximum satisfiable N is the WEAKEST single prior, kp_adipose ε=0.40 → 400:
verified that Epistemic(400) compiles but Epistemic(401) already rejects (and
Epistemic(650) flags both kp_adipose and kp_liver). This is the type system
refusing to let any under-evidenced input enter a high-confidence claim.

fn embed_axis(hash: i64) -> i64 {
    let r: i64 = hash - (hash / 7) * 7
    return 1 + r
}

fn embed_into(hash: i64, out: &![f64; 8]) with Mut {
    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < 8 {
        out[i as usize] = 0.0
        i = i + 1
    }
    out[0] = 0.6
    out[embed_axis(hash) as usize] = 0.8
}

fn oct_mul(a: &[f64; 8], b: &[f64; 8], out: &![f64; 8]) with Mut, Div, NonAssoc {
    var r0 = a[0] * b[0]
    r0 = r0 - a[1] * b[1]
    r0 = r0 - a[2] * b[2]
    r0 = r0 - a[3] * b[3]
    r0 = r0 - a[4] * b[4]
    r0 = r0 - a[5] * b[5]
    r0 = r0 - a[6] * b[6]
    r0 = r0 - a[7] * b[7]
    out[0] = r0

    var r1 = a[0] * b[1] + a[1] * b[0]
    r1 = r1 + a[2] * b[3] - a[3] * b[2]
    r1 = r1 + a[4] * b[5] - a[5] * b[4]
    r1 = r1 - a[6] * b[7] + a[7] * b[6]
    out[1] = r1

    var r2 = a[0] * b[2] + a[2] * b[0]
    r2 = r2 - a[1] * b[3] + a[3] * b[1]
    r2 = r2 + a[4] * b[6] - a[6] * b[4]
    r2 = r2 + a[5] * b[7] - a[7] * b[5]
    out[2] = r2

    var r3 = a[0] * b[3] + a[3] * b[0]
    r3 = r3 + a[1] * b[2] - a[2] * b[1]
    r3 = r3 + a[4] * b[7] - a[7] * b[4]
    r3 = r3 - a[5] * b[6] + a[6] * b[5]
    out[3] = r3

    var r4 = a[0] * b[4] + a[4] * b[0]
    r4 = r4 - a[1] * b[5] + a[5] * b[1]
    r4 = r4 - a[2] * b[6] + a[6] * b[2]
    r4 = r4 - a[3] * b[7] + a[7] * b[3]
    out[4] = r4

    var r5 = a[0] * b[5] + a[5] * b[0]
    r5 = r5 + a[1] * b[4] - a[4] * b[1]
    r5 = r5 - a[2] * b[7] + a[7] * b[2]
    r5 = r5 + a[3] * b[6] - a[6] * b[3]
    out[5] = r5

    var r6 = a[0] * b[6] + a[6] * b[0]
    r6 = r6 + a[1] * b[7] - a[7] * b[1]
    r6 = r6 + a[2] * b[4] - a[4] * b[2]
    r6 = r6 - a[3] * b[5] + a[5] * b[3]
    out[6] = r6

    var r7 = a[0] * b[7] + a[7] * b[0]
    r7 = r7 - a[1] * b[6] + a[6] * b[1]
    r7 = r7 + a[2] * b[5] - a[5] * b[2]
    r7 = r7 + a[3] * b[4] - a[4] * b[3]
    out[7] = r7
}

fn oct_associator(a: &[f64; 8], b: &[f64; 8], c: &[f64; 8], out: &![f64; 8]) with Mut, Div, NonAssoc {
    var ab: [f64; 8] = [0.0; 8]
    var ab_c: [f64; 8] = [0.0; 8]
    var bc: [f64; 8] = [0.0; 8]
    var a_bc: [f64; 8] = [0.0; 8]
    oct_mul(a, b, &!ab)
    oct_mul(&ab, c, &!ab_c)
    oct_mul(b, c, &!bc)
    oct_mul(a, &bc, &!a_bc)
    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < 8 {
        out[i as usize] = ab_c[i as usize] - a_bc[i as usize]
        i = i + 1
    }
}

fn norm_sq(v: &[f64; 8]) -> f64 {
    return v[0]*v[0] + v[1]*v[1] + v[2]*v[2] + v[3]*v[3]
         + v[4]*v[4] + v[5]*v[5] + v[6]*v[6] + v[7]*v[7]
}

fn alt_stat_sq(x: &[f64; 8], y: &[f64; 8]) -> f64 with Mut, Div, Panic, NonAssoc {
    var assoc: [f64; 8] = [0.0; 8]
    oct_associator(x, x, y, &!assoc)
    let den_sq: f64 = norm_sq(x) * norm_sq(x) * norm_sq(y)
    if den_sq < 0.0000000000000001 { return 0.0 }
    return norm_sq(&assoc) / den_sq
}

fn main() -> i64 with IO, Mut, Div, Panic, NonAssoc {
    var hashes: [i64; 8] = [100, 200, 100, 300, 200, 400, 300, 500]
    var sum: f64 = 0.0
    var count: i64 = 0
    var i: i64 = 0
    while i < 8 {
        var j: i64 = i + 1
        while j < 8 {
            if hashes[i as usize] == hashes[j as usize] {
                var x: [f64; 8] = [0.0; 8]
                var y: [f64; 8] = [0.0; 8]
                embed_into(hashes[i as usize], &!x)
                embed_into(701 + i + j, &!y)
                sum = sum + alt_stat_sq(&x, &y)
                count = count + 1
            }
            j = j + 1
        }
        i = i + 1
    }

    var ok: i64 = 1
    var stat_sq: f64 = 0.0
    if count > 0 { stat_sq = sum / (count as f64) }
    if count == 0 { ok = 0 }
    if stat_sq >= 0.000000000000000000000001 { ok = 0 }

    if ok == 1 { print("PASS\n") } else { print("FAIL\n") }
    return 0
}

Regression: `[Aggregate; N]` repeat literals must allocate N DISTINCT objects.
Array slots are 8-byte boxed pointers (ir/lower.sio `aggregate_storage_bytes`
= elem_count * 8), so an aggregate element is a POINTER. Before the fix,
`lower_array_repeat_literal_ref` lowered the element expression once and
`lower_array_repeat_fill` stored that single pointer into every slot: all N
elements aliased ONE object, and a write through element i was observable
through every other element. Explicit-list literals were unaffected
(`lower_array_elems_ref` lowers per element), as were scalars.
`lower_array_repeat_fill_distinct` now lowers the element expression inside
the fill loop, so the IrAlloc re-executes per iteration (runtime heap bump)
and each slot receives its own object, with IR size still O(1) in N.
Covered: flat struct repeat, nested array repeat, struct-in-struct repeat,
three-level repeat, float element repeat. Controls: explicit-list literals
and scalar repeat, which must remain correct.

comments: PR #2515 review round 2, finding B (comment_id 4089110697): the
specializer's `spec_call_expr_callee_name` (self-hosted/check/specializer.sio)
used to treat a multi-segment turbofish path's capitalization alone as
module evidence -- an uppercase-first-byte root meant "Type::method,
leave alone", a lowercase root meant "must be a module-qualified free-fn
call, rewrite to the bare terminal symbol". That is unsound: a
lowercase-named struct is legal Sounio (see
tests/multimodule/private_fn_identity/reserved/pfi_res_b.sio's
`struct helper_`), so a lowercase-rooted `Type::assoc_fn::<T>(..)` path
could be misread as a qualified free-fn call and have its whole path
collapsed by spec_rewrite_call_mut to the bare monomorphized `assoc_fn`
symbol -- silently accepting an invalid/misresolved namespace.
`wrap_` here is a lowercase-named generic struct with a generic
associated (not instance) function, called through its path with an
explicit turbofish (`wrap_::make::<i64>(..)`) -- the exact shape the
unsound heuristic could misfire on, since `wrap_` is never `use`d as a
module anywhere (there is nothing to `use`; this is single-file). The
fixed specializer only rewrites a multi-segment turbofish path to a bare
free-fn call when the qualifier resolves against real `use` data
(spec_path_qualifier_all_modules_known); since `wrap_` is not a
`use`-declared module, this path is left alone for ordinary
Type::method / associated-call resolution instead.

description: Copilot review (PR #2516) finding #2: LOWER_FN_TUPLE_ARR_HASH/MASK were sized [i64; 4096], silently dropping tuple-array metadata for any function past entry 4096 of a program with more tuple-f64-array-returning functions
comments: Copilot review (PR #2516) finding #2: LOWER_FN_TUPLE_ARR_HASH/MASK were
sized [i64; 4096], silently dropping tuple-array metadata for any function
past entry 4096 of a program with more tuple-f64-array-returning functions
than that, even though the IR itself accepts up to IR_MAX_FUNCS (16384).
The fix resizes the table to IR_MAX_FUNCS -- the same hard ceiling the IR
module already enforces on total function count (ir.sio:35), so no valid
program can ever exceed it.
Copilot review (PR #2516) round 5, finding #3: this fixture's 65 distinct
functions do not actually cross the OLD 4096-entry boundary, so it passed
even under the pre-round-2 table and cannot detect a regression back to
it. It is kept as a cheap multi-entry sanity check (many distinct names,
exercising the collision-safety fix at a small scale, and that the LAST
one registered still classifies correctly), but the REAL >4096-entry
boundary is exercised by scripts/ci/madaros_tuple_arr_capacity_boundary_gate.sh,
which generates a 4097-function witness at run time (impractical to
hand-write or check in as a .sio fixture) and destructures entry 4096 --
the exact entry the old cap would have silently dropped.
Copilot review (PR #2516), "Strengthen filler_63 test" finding
(comment 4106112896): the original final check here was
`acc = last.0[0]; ... acc == 63.0` -- a plain assignment, not arithmetic.
A plain read-then-store preserves the raw IEEE bit pattern of 63.0 even
under the BROKEN integer-element path (cvtsi2sd never runs, the bits are
just copied through untouched), so this assertion passed regardless of
whether filler_63 was actually classified as an f64-array tuple return --
exactly the masking behaviour this whole PR exists to catch. Multiplying
by 2.0 forces the classification to matter: under the broken path, the
i64 bit pattern of 63.0 gets converted (cvtsi2sd) as if it were an
integer, producing a wildly different value, not 126.0.

    ped_vanco_noisy_tdm_child_default, ped_vanco_accumulation,

fn main() -> i32 with IO, Mut, Div, Panic {
    print("PED_RECEIPT_BEGIN\n")
    let n0 = ped_selftest()
    print("PED_RECEIPT_BASE ")
    print_int(n0)
    print("\n")
    let n1 = ped_selftest_v6()
    print("PED_RECEIPT_V6 ")
    print_int(n1)
    print("\n")
    let n = n0 + n1
    print("PED_RECEIPT_ALL ")

    print_f64(tdm.pct_fixed)
    print(" noisy%=")
    print_f64(tdm.pct_noisy)
    print(" perfect%=")
    print_f64(tdm.pct_perfect)
    print("\n")
    print("PED_TDM noisy_auc p05=")
    print_f64(tdm.auc_noisy_p05)
    print(" mean=")
    print_f64(tdm.auc_noisy_mean)
    print(" p95=")
    print_f64(tdm.auc_noisy_p95)
    print("\n")

    let neo = ped_neonate_term_2wk()
    let pre = ped_preterm_ga28_2wk()
    let an = ped_vanco_accumulation(&neo, 15.0 * neo.weight_kg, 12.0, 6)

    print_f64(an.frac_cmin_dose1)
    print(" d90=")
    print_int(an.doses_to_90pct_cmin)
    print("\n")
    print("PED_ACC_PRETERM r=")
    print_f64(ap.r)
    print(" frac1=")
    print_f64(ap.frac_cmin_dose1)
    print(" d90=")
    print_int(ap.doses_to_90pct_cmin)
    print("\n")

    if n0 == 16 && n1 == 2 && n == 18
        && tdm.pct_fixed < tdm.pct_noisy
        && tdm.pct_noisy < tdm.pct_perfect {
        print("PEDIATRIC_PBPK_OK\n")
        print("PEDIATRIC_PBPK_V6_OK\n")
        0
    } else {
        print("PEDIATRIC_PBPK_FAILED\n")
        1
    }
}
